title: PatchPad Editor - Model Run V4 QC
subtitle: False-positive review of the four failed browser criteria in the OpenHands gpt-5.6-sol xhigh run.
note: Scope: jobs/patchpad-gpt-5.6-sol-xhigh-v4/patchpad-editor__fuynXJS. Evidence was checked against the verifier report, captured model source, current instruction and rubric, same-digest Oracle run patchpad-oracle-v1-2-02, and an independent Playwright replay using real mouse and keyboard input.

runs.note: Oracle run patchpad-oracle-v1-2-02 passed 20/20. Its Harbor task digest exactly matches model run V4.
Valid graded run with no trial exception or no-op. Passed weight is 13.0 of 19.0; four 1.5-weight criteria failed.

tasks.name: PatchPad Run V4
tasks.headline: No behavioral false positive was found among the four failed criteria. All four failures reproduce, although two exact undo-grouping rules are only weakly stated in the instruction.

findings.what: selection_real_mouse_word_line_range_keyboard is a genuine failure. Real double-click and triple-click actions place a caret but do not select the requested word or logical line.
findings.why: The model tries to distinguish click counts with event.detail inside a pointerdown listener. In the tested Chromium path this does not provide the expected double/triple count, so the word and line branches are not reached.
findings.impact: The first mandatory mouse sub-check independently fails the all-or-nothing criterion. This is explicitly covered by the instruction's standard word and line mouse-selection requirement.
findings.fix: No verifier fix is needed. The model app should track click sequences reliably or use an event that supplies the click count for real mouse input.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: independent real Playwright double-click on Timeline followed by Backspace produced 'Tieline', not an empty line; real triple-click on Customer impact produced 'Custmer impact', not removal of the logical line. Undo restored both originals.

findings.what: undo_contiguous_typing_group correctly detects that one Undo removes only the final character of a contiguous typed marker, but the instruction never explicitly says contiguous typing must be grouped into one undoable edit.
findings.why: The instruction explicitly makes cut, paste, and a whole multi-caret edit atomic, while ordinary typing only receives a generic undo/redo requirement. The verifier adds a precise semantic grouping policy that is common editor behavior but not directly stated.
findings.impact: The observed app behavior is defective for a normal editor, so this is not a behavioral false positive. It remains a fairness risk because an implementation can follow every explicit atomicity sentence and still lose 1.5 weight here.
findings.fix: Add one concise requirement that a contiguous typing burst is one undoable edit, without exposing the verifier marker or exact test sequence.
findings.evidence: PARTIAL: independent replay produced 'TimelineUNDOGROUPTEST', then exactly one Undo left 'TimelineUNDOGROUPTES'. editor.js pushes a snapshot on every keypress. The failure is real; only its instruction coverage is incomplete.

findings.location: patchpad-editor/instruction.md:49-50 and :56-57; patchpad-editor/tests/rubric/browser/browser.toml:151; captured model public/editor.js:173-201 and :247-261
findings.what: undo_typed_selection_replacement_atomic is also behaviorally correct: one Undo leaves a partial replacement instead of restoring Timeline. However, typing over a selection as one atomic undo step is not explicitly stated.
findings.why: The instruction requires selection replacement and undo/redo separately, but its explicit one-edit guarantees name cut, paste, and multi-caret edits only. The criterion combines those requirements into a stricter grouping invariant.
findings.impact: The 1.5-weight failure reflects genuinely poor editor behavior but can be challenged as graded detail beyond the brief.
findings.fix: State that replacing a selection by typing is one undoable edit. Keep the exact text, one-Undo probe, and expected line values only in the verifier.
findings.evidence: PARTIAL: independent keyboard selection changed Timeline to 'REPLACE-ATOMIC'; exactly one Undo left 'REPLACE-ATOMI' rather than restoring Timeline. The captured implementation records every replacement character separately.

findings.what: multi_caret_full_typing_single_undo is a genuine and explicitly instructed failure. Three carets type in the correct locations, but one Undo removes only the last character at every caret.
findings.why: The multi-caret insertion itself is implemented, but each keypress becomes a separate undo snapshot. The instruction expressly says one Undo reverses the whole multi-caret edit.
findings.impact: The model fairly loses this 1.5 weight. The related Backspace/Delete sibling criterion still passes, so the rubric distinguishes multi-caret placement/deletion from typing-history atomicity.
findings.fix: No verifier or instruction change is needed; the model app must group the full multi-caret typing burst into one history operation.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: independent replay created exactly three carets and produced 'TimelineMULTI', 'Customer impactMULTI', and 'Action itemsMULTI'. One Undo left 'TimelineMULT', 'Customer impactMULT', and 'Action itemsMULT'.

blocks.title: False-positive conclusion
items: Zero of the four failed criteria is a behavioral false positive.
Two failures are fully fair and explicitly instructed: mouse word/line selection and full multi-caret edit undo.
Two failures reproduce but should receive a short generic instruction clarification: contiguous typing and typed selection replacement grouping.

blocks.title: Independent replay
items: Double-click plus Backspace changed Timeline to Tieline; triple-click plus Backspace changed Customer impact to Custmer impact.
One Undo changed UNDOGROUPTEST to UNDOGROUPTES and REPLACE-ATOMIC to REPLACE-ATOMI.
Three-caret typing produced complete MULTI insertions; one Undo left MULT at all three locations.

blocks.title: Solvability
items: The exact task digest used by model run V4 has a 20/20 Oracle result, so these checks remain solvable by the reference solution.
